click.text: Ah, right. Mugwort Fleuries and matches, please.

options.text: How's the parish surviving without its holy music box?
You really let a walking fuck-up do church stuff?

raph.text: "Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness."
...I can hear the disapproval in your voice, child. You're not the first to rehearse it for me.
But you know, God's never had much trouble using the broken ones for the sake of something better. The ones who sometimes shout, flip tables and show up to Mass with a black eye.
...He's good with a shovel, heavy things, and breaking up fights at ceremonies. With the kind of tasks no one wants to talk about, but someone always has to do, to keep the holy façade from cracking.
That's... not exactly what they teach at seminary, but out here, it gets the job done.

mass.text: Ah, the organ... We left it silent. No hymns, no chords to fill the air. No background noise, as you said.
Every Agnus Dei, every Sanctus, every place where the organ should sing... We let Him speak instead. Even the readings - we murmured them barely above breath, or said nothing at all.
It was unsettling at first, you could hear everything. The rain tapping the windows. Postman's knees cracking like dry twigs. Babette's stomach growling during the Eucharist.
But soon, the silence started feeling warm and gentle. People breathed slower. They began to move like they were part of the silence, not fighting it. Nobody hurried.
And I thought... maybe He finally had room to answer.

mass_silenceno.text: Oh, you know, I've been thinking about what you said last time.
On Wednesday, the silence felt... too bare. People sat still, but their faces seemed so distant. Postman's knees cracking like dry twigs. Babette's stomach growling during the Eucharist.

guitar.text: So I bought a guitar. Brought it yesterday and just played a few soft chords here and there, between the readings. Just a little help to carry the words forward.

guitar_bellowsAsked.text: So I had this small idea... nothing big, just a little help to carry the words forward. And to my surprise, Yves agreed to it.
I bought a guitar. Yves brought his clarinet and sat beside me... quieter than usual.
We played a few small things here and there, between the readings.

massEnd.text: People's faces became softer, their eyes started smiling. And at that moment... I knew God had been humming with us too.

checkout.text: Thank you. Off to see if the house of God is still occupied.

entry.text: It's still here! It's been hanging around all weekend, and I literally just saw it galumphing around the church on my way here.
Seriously, promise me you'll read the paper when I leave. I'm basically half the editorial team at this point, so, you know... give it some love.
Oh, and a pack of red Morleys, and some chewing tobacco, please.

options.text: And what's the seal doing there?

response.text: Not much. Flops from one spot to another, barks at random, then just takes another nap.
People keep stopping to stare at it, though. Like it's going to get up and... I don't know, do something big?
But for now, it just... exists.
Well, chew is for Eel Lady. I don't even need fish anymore, but it's kind of impossible to say no once she decides you're useful.
And Morleys are for my mum. Sadly.
But... I mean, I've been thinking about it. I love the idea of it - the little rituals and quiet pauses between words and the way people lean in closer just because of a cigarette.
Drifting smoke and cigarette holders... Super chic.
I keep telling myself I'll start, like, next week or whatever... I even plan it out sometimes - the perfect moment, the perfect lighter.

options.text: Where did that paper come from?

response.text: Someone left it for me at the newsroom. No name, no return address, just that little treasure map and a bit of blood. Enough to get my attention.
Inside that left side? A whole damned labyrinth. Papers, notebooks, matchboxes, tins, weird little wrapped things - all crammed between pipes or pushed into cavities.
A stash? Some kind of postal system? God knows how long I was in there, elbows deep, trying to figure out what the hell the place even was.
And then - bang - something cracked me on the back of the head. Ears ringing. Floor tilting. Lights out.
Woke up on a pew with Father Jean-Noël rehearsing some sermon draft over me. For a second I thought that was it. Purgatory.

Later... When I finally got another chance to look, the notes, the parcels, the whole delicious mess were already gone. I pulled out half the pipes on that side trying to find even one scrap, but nothing.
Oh. Right. That. When I got knocked out, I'm pretty sure I saw the hem of an altar boy's surplice in the corner of my eye.
And, well... we've got one rather questionable altar boy who 1) has a history of hitting people, 2) is chronically allergic to me, but 3) used to eat sand pies with you.

...Honestly, after the stash evaporated and nothing else twitched for months, I just let the whole thing fade out of my brain. But then with everything bubbling again lately, I thought, hey, maybe the thread isn't dead after all.
Except now, without evidence or the one person I hoped to grill... I've got... nothing, really. No scenario left to act out.
Okay, look... I tried to put everything back how I found it... Ish. I mean, the thing still played at the next Mass, so I convinced myself it was fine.
In my defence, the place was already a mess. I thought if I nudged a few pipes out of place, it wouldn't matter. Like... what's one more crime in a crime scene?
...That's not great, isn't it?
*sigh*
Okay, I'll... sort something out. Make up for this little vandalism somehow.
Nah, don't think so. Looks like one of last year's pups, around nine, ten months maybe. That's old enough to know the way back.
Though I did see the nuns trying to guide it to the sea, waving their arms like shepherds. Cutest thing I've ever seen.
I thought so when it ignored the fish I brought. Then it gobbled the same fish off another hand. So it's fine.
...Next time it'll be me.
Check out my article and you'll see, silly.

response.text: Huh? We're not a gang. We're a pod, like theals. Gangth do thtupid thtuff like leadership thtructures and profit motiveth. Jutht like adultth.
Theals don't do that crap. No name tag, no thocial statuth, no comfy little cage to sit in. Jutht fat and buoyant.

That maketh adults twitchy. Dithoriented. They can't help but drift toward it and thpill whatever bullthit they've got in their brain. Deregulated thalvation, that'th the thervice the creature provideth.
The pod jutht wanth to keep thtupid people from messing with it too much. Phythically and theoretically. So the lethon stayth clean.
In the end we're pupilth too. Thtill learning how not to ruin it ourthelveth. Thtill figuring out what a proper pod even lookth like.
Menthol JC and four toffeeth. Pleathe.

entry.text: Hey...
I thought... maybe you wouldn't judge me if I asked you.

It's just- I- I've had this thing for a while now. And I keep thinking, maybe I shouldn't have taken it, maybe I should give it back. But it's been too long, and maybe it'd only make everything messier. And I don't even know why I'm bringing it up now, it's just- you seem...

...like someone who wouldn't laugh. Or make it worse. Or tell everyone. And I'm not, like, a hundred percent sure who I took it from. More like... eighty? Eighty-five, maybe. It was dark, it was rushed, I was so tired, and... I mean, I'm not asking you to, like, investigate...

...or whatever. I mean you don't have to. Just... if by chance, I don't know, if something clicks and you just know, then... maybe. But also, maybe not. Maybe I even want it to stay here so I can pretend I tried, but still keep it.

If it works out, great. If not, I'll take it back and we'll pretend this never happened. Gosh. Sorry. This is probably a terrible idea but... ugh. I'll just leave it here. Okay. That's it. I'm- yeah. Bye.
